item.title: Metric dimension and maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of graph Laplacians
item.description: arXiv:2610.26875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study equality between metric dimension and the maximum eigenvalue multiplicity of the Laplacian and signless Laplacian matrices. These quantities are not ordered in general. Using the standard decomposition associated with twin classes, we separate forced multiplicities from quotient-spectrum contributions. We give complete equality classifications for complete multipartite graphs and core--satellite graphs, and enumerate the multipartite equality graphs by order. For graphs formed by attaching at least two leaves to every vertex of a connected core, the metric dimension and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $ 1 $ are known; we show that this multiplicity is maximal for both matrices, and uniquely maximal except for $ P_3 $. We enumerate this core--leaf family up to isomorphism and obtain a uniform asymptotic formula by order and metric dimension, together with the quadratic exponential growth rate $ 1/18 $. An exact census of connected graphs of orders two through seven identifies the first separating examples and examples without twins. Finally, for every odd $ r \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 3} $, we study $ \Theta_{2, 2, r} $ and determine both maximum multiplicities: the two equality properties alternate with $ r $ modulo four, producing infinite separating families in both directions.
item.dc:creator: Monther Rashed Alfuraidan, Suliman Khan, Lorenzo Sauras Altuzarra

item.title: A positivity conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton
item.description: arXiv:2610.26878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton (2003) that $\frac{1-q}{(q^n;q)_m}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{n}{m}_{q}$ has nonnegative power-series coefficients for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. We obtain a polynomial version by bounding a M\"obius correction by first differences of Gaussian coefficients. The proof uses partitions and quadratic and cubic semi-invariants of binary forms. An extension of this bound proves the Reiner--Stanton--White conjecture on positivity of orbit polynomials for flags of subspaces.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Prellberg

item.title: Vertex Removal and Vertex-Edge Domination
item.description: arXiv:2610.26912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ $ve$-dominates every edge incident with a vertex in its closed neighborhood $N_{G}[v]$. A set of vertices is a vertex-edge dominating set ($ve$-dominating set) if every edge of $G$ is $ve$-dominated by some vertex in the set. The minimum cardinality of such a set is the vertex-edge domination number $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, also known as the isolation number. In this paper, we study the effect of vertex removal on $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, establish sharp bounds on $\gamma_{ve}(G-v)$ and characterize the vertices whose removal decreases, preserves, or increases $\gamma_{ve}(G)$. Let $V^0(G)$ and $V^+(G)$ denote the sets of vertices whose removal preserves and increases $\gamma_{ve}(G)$, respectively, and let $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ consist of the vertices in $V^0(G)$ belonging to every minimum $ve$-dominating set. We prove that \[ |V^0(G)|\geq3|V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)|+\sum_{v\in V^+(G)} \bigl(\gamma_{ve}(G-v)-\gamma_{ve}(G)+1\bigr). \] In particular, $|V^0(G)|\geq 2|V^+(G)|$. We also prove that every vertex in $V_{\mathrm{fix}}^0(G)$ lies on a cycle and that $V^0(T)\neq\emptyset$ for every tree $T$ of order at least three.
item.dc:creator: Minhui Li, Shumin Zhang, Fengming Dong

item.title: Gaussian Lower Bounds for Distinct Subset Sums in Higher Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For sequences of $n$ nonnegative integer vectors in $\mathbb Z^k$ with distinct subset sums, we prove, for fixed $k$, the uniform lower bound $M\ge (C_k-o(1))2^{n/k}/\sqrt n$ for the largest coordinate, where \[ C_k=\sqrt{\frac{2k}{\pi}}\, \frac{(k+1)^{(k-1)/(2k)}}{\sqrt{\lfloor (k+1)^2/4\rfloor}}. \] The proof compares a Gaussian-kernel expectation with a sum over a translated lattice, uniformly over the vector sequence. We optimise the resulting quadratic-form constant using a vertex second-moment certificate. We show that $C_k$ also exceeds the variance constant obtained by optimising an ellipsoidal geometry.
item.dc:creator: Zijie Gu

item.title: Partitionability is NP-complete
item.description: arXiv:2610.27083v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the problem of deciding whether a simplicial complex is partitionable is NP-complete in dimensions two and higher, answering a 1995 question of Kleinschmidt and Onn.
item.dc:creator: Russ Woodroofe

item.title: Tree Lattices and the Neumann-Zagier conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27095v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A tree with integer weights on its vertices presents an integral lattice called a tree lattice. We prove that if a tree lattice is positive definite, then one of the vertex elements is irreducible, i.e. determines a facet of its Voronoi polyhedron. As a corollary, we settle a 1985 conjecture of Neumann and Zagier: if a tree lattice is isometric to the lattice of integer points in Euclidean space, then the tree contains a vertex of weight one.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Evan Greene, Ahmad Issa, Duncan McCoy

item.title: Subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27117v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Since their introduction by Karo\'nski, Scheinerman, and Singer-Cohen in 90's, random intersection graphs have attracted much attention, mostly due to their various applications. In this article, we establish a general result for the probability that a given small subgraph is present in a random intersection graph. Our theorem applies to a broad range of parameters, including regimes that have not previously been considered in the literature. Moreover, it extends known results and situates them within a broader framework, making this approach a convenient tool for comparing the probabilities of graphs in the random intersection graph model. To prove our main result, we develop new proof techniques that, to the best of our knowledge, have not previously been employed in the study of small subgraphs in random intersection graphs. Many special cases and examples are presented as well.
item.dc:creator: Katarzyna Rybarczyk, Grzegorz Serafin

item.title: Normal approximation for subgraph counts in random intersection graphs: the case of cliques
item.description: arXiv:2610.27128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $X^{(r)}_n$ denote the number of copies of a complete graph $K_r$ in the random intersection graph model on $n$ vertices. We derive upper bounds on the distance between the standardized version of $X^{(r)}_n$ and the standard normal distribution, measured in both the Kolmogorov and Wasserstein metrics. We complement these results with necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic normality. As a byproduct, we provide precise estimates for the variance of $X^{(r)}_n$. In the process, we develop new general techniques for analysing so--called clique covers, which play a crucial role in the study of subgraph probabilities in random intersection graphs.
item.dc:creator: Katarzyna Rybarczyk, Grzegorz Serafin

item.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture and improved bounds for bipanchromatic colorings
item.description: arXiv:2610.27133v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the bipanchromatic number $\chi_B$, introduced by Lalou et al. (Discrete Appl. Math. 391 (2026), 511-522) as the maximum number of colors in a panchromatic hypergraph coloring where every color appears at least twice. They show that merging uniquely occurring colors in a maximum panchromatic coloring gives the lower bound $\beta=\chi_P-\lceil\alpha/2\rceil \leq \chi_B$, where $\chi_P$ is the panchromatic number and $\alpha$ is the minimum number of such colors among maximum panchromatic colorings. They conjectured that $\chi_B=\beta$ and subsequently disproved it (arXiv:2610.08042). We identify the smallest counterexample, with six vertices and three hyperedges, both minimum possible. We show that the ratio bound $\chi_B/\beta<2$ is asymptotically sharp and prove minimality results for the order and hyperedge count. For $3\le\alpha<\chi_P$ we show that every integer from $\beta$ to $\chi_P-1$ occurs as $\chi_B$ while $\chi_P$ and $\alpha$ are held fixed. Furthermore, we discover that the values $|V|,\chi_P,\alpha$ directly decide whether the conjectured equality holds except when $\alpha=4$, where a matching reduction resolves the ambiguity. We derive the optimal universal lower bound $L$ depending only on $|V|,\chi_P,\alpha$ in the nontrivial regime $0<2\alpha<|V|$. Finally, we prove $\chi_B/L\le5/4$ and $\chi_B/L\le6/5+1/(5L)$, with $5/4$ sharp and $6/5$ asymptotically sharp as $L\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Novakovi\'c, Du\v{s}ko Joji\'c

item.title: Recent progress in the construction of Hadamard matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.27175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Hadamard matrix is a square matrix with entries $\pm 1$ whose rows are mutually orthogonal. Hadamard matrices are conjectured to exist at every order divisible by $4$; for approximately the last twenty years, the smallest open case of this conjecture was order 668. In August 2026, Alp\"oge, Voinov and Reynolds-Haertle announced Hadamard matrices at the twelve orders below $2000$ at which none was known. In this paper we verify and analyse the claimed matrices. We survey results on the existence of Hadamard matrices and list the $95$ orders up to $10\,000$ at which no Hadamard matrix is currently known. In pursuing this work we constructed Hadamard matrices at sixteen orders that were open in the published literature. We conclude with a list of open problems.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Egan, Ilias Kotsireas, Stephen London, P\'adraig \'O Cath\'ain

item.title: Total $\{k\}$-domination in caterpillars: Structural properties and exact results
item.description: arXiv:2610.27181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The total $\{k\}$-domination problem ($T\{k\}DP$) seeks a minimum-weight function such that the sum of weights in every open neighborhood is at least $k$. While this problem is known to be NP-hard for general graphs, we demonstrate that for the family of caterpillars, it simplifies to the classical total domination number ($k=1$) via the identity $\gamma^{\{k\}}_t(G) = k\gamma_t(G)$. This reduction is supported by a general upper bound established for all graphs, which we prove to be tight specifically for caterpillars. The central tool for our analysis is the introduction of a $(T,R)$-representation, a one-to-one mapping that abstracts caterpillar structure into discrete vectors based on support vertex distribution and central path segment lengths. By characterizing these segments through congruence modulo 4, we derive an exact closed-form expression for the total $\{k\}$-domination number of any caterpillar graph.
item.dc:creator: Mariana Escalante, Paola Tolomei, Mar\'ia In\'es Lopez Pujato

item.title: A Pittel-type limit law for the largest component of random $d$-uniform hypergraphs: enumeration and excursions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H_d(n,M)$ be a $d$-uniform hypergraph with $n$ vertices and $M$ hyperedges. In the critical window $M=\frac{n}{d(d-1)}(1+\lambda n^{-1/3})+O(1)$, its largest component $L_n$ satisfies $$n^{-2/3}L_n\xrightarrow{\mathcal L} \mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}\bigl((d-1)^{1/3}a,\lambda(d-1)^{-2/3}\bigr).$$ (Here $\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{Pit}}(x,\mu)$ denotes the limiting law of the largest component of the critical random graph established by Pittel (2001).) The proof rests on two pillars. First, a bivariate exponential formula gives the exact finite-size law of $L_n$. Subsequently, cancellation of the orders $n,n^{2/3},n^{1/3}$ in the tree normalization determines the series of rooted hypertrees, then that of unicyclic components and its singular expansions at the radius of convergence $\rho_d$. These calculations are exact; they serve the fixed-excess identities and the cancellation mechanism, and nothing more: no unproved uniformity in the excess enters the proof of the limit law. Next, by exploration and martingale approximation, the ordered sizes converge unconditionally to the excursion lengths of a Brownian motion with parabolic drift. A monotone coupling transfers the law to $H_d(n,M)$. The limit law is then identified with Pittel's law by a Brownian rescaling: if $h=d-1$, it suffices to multiply lengths by $h^{-1/3}$ and evaluate at parameter $\lambda h^{-2/3}$. The exact Poisson representation dispenses with any separate deconditioning. We also formulate a two-regime $d$-uniform Bollobas bound (Wright for fixed $\ell$, global combinatorial beyond that), and explicitly indicate why neither regime alone suffices to close the analytic route.
item.dc:creator: Youssouf Wirdane

item.title: PL standardness of the four-pentachoron census sphere Q
item.description: arXiv:2610.27283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the four-pentachoron homotopy \(4\)-sphere \(Q\) singled out in the census of Burke, Burton and Spreer is PL homeomorphic to the standard \(4\)-sphere. The key construction identifies the compact exterior of an explicit locally flat \(2\)-sphere in an auxiliary 39-vertex model of \(Q\) with the exterior of Budney, Burton and Hillman, then certifies its fibration by a normal cut followed by a relative collapse. The exterior identification uses finite checked moves, an exact regular-neighbourhood construction and a PL lemma controlling the passage through an ideal triangulation. Cutting the compact exterior along the specified normal hypersurface gives a manifold that collapses onto one boundary copy of the punctured \(3\)-torus in 209,144 elementary pairs; a marked product lemma identifies the cut as a product. The resulting integral monodromy realizes \(Q\) as a Cappell--Shaneson filling whose two surgery framings are standard by Gompf's results. The fibration certificate is independent of Issa's earlier PL-compatible constructions. Combined with the published census, the result establishes standardness for every homotopy \(4\)-sphere triangulated with at most four pentachora.
item.dc:creator: Vance Faber, Michael Murphy

item.title: A Solution to the Kohayakawa-Pr\"omel-R\"odl Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.27478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)$ is defined as the minimum order of a graph $F$ such that any 2-coloring of its edges with red and blue leads to either a red induced copy of $G$ or a blue induced copy of $H$. In 1998, Kohayakawa, Pr\"omel, and R\"odl conjectured that for any fixed graph $G$, there exists a constant $f=f(G)$ such that the induced Ramsey number $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G, H)$ is bounded by $|V(H)|^f$ for every graph $H$. In this paper, we completely solve the Kohayakawa--Pr\"omel--R\"odl conjecture, which states that for any graphs $G$ and $H$ with $|V(G)|=k\ge2$ and $|V(H)|=t\ge2$, $r_{\mathrm{ind}}(G,H)\le t^{60k^2+3}$. This verifies the conjecture with $f(G)=60|V(G)|^2+3$.
item.dc:creator: Chuang Zhong, Masaki Kashima, Yaping Mao

item.title: On Entries of Spectral Decompositions and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The entries of the spectral idempotents of a graph are its local and crossed local multiplicities. This paper uses these classical quantities in three applications. First, in a graph on $n$ vertices without isolated vertices, every local multiplicity is at most $\frac{n-1}{n}$, and every diagonal entry of the Cesaro average mixing matrix is at most $1-\frac{2}{n}+\frac{2}{n^2}$. In both bounds equality holds only for the complete graph. This proves the connected form of the complete graph trace conjecture of Godsil, Guo and Sobchuk together with its equality case, and component and degree refinements follow. The two upper bounds and their attainment by complete graphs also occur in a recent machine checked proof, without a formal characterization of when equality holds. Second, for the line graph of a connected graph $\Gamma$, the average return probability at a bridge with a bipartite component on one side is at least the reciprocal of the rank of the unsigned incidence matrix. Equality holds exactly for $P_2$ and $P_3$. The proof combines local moments with known inverse-incidence formulas. Finally, the paper gives a short proof of Godsil's entry criterion, which says that vertices $u$ and $v$ are strongly cospectral exactly when $\left|(E_\theta)_{uv}\right|=(E_\theta)_{uu}$ for every eigenvalue $\theta$. The criterion recovers the known classification in connected noncomplete strongly regular graphs, where the strongly cospectral pairs are precisely the two-vertex parts of cocktail party graphs.
item.dc:creator: Musung Kang

item.title: The achromatic number of Paley graphs, Peisert graphs, and related Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The achromatic number of a graph $G$, denoted $\chi_a (G)$, is the maximum number of colors in a proper vertex coloring of $G$. Generalizing a result of Maistrelli and Penman, we prove that for sufficiently large $q$, the achromatic number of the $k$-th power Paley graph is at least $\frac{q-1}{k} + 1$. This lower bound gives the correct order of magnitude in $q$, but determining the correct dependence on $k$ remains open for all $k \geq 3$. The achromatic number of Peisert graphs is shown to be $\frac{q+1}{2}$. These bounds are consequences of a general theorem involving Cayley graphs whose generating set is a union of cyclotomic classes. Using character sums and Weil's bound, we prove an upper bound that improves the standard trivial bound $\binom{ \chi_a (G) }{2} \leq e(G)$. Finally, we consider random Cayley-sum graphs on an abelian group $\Gamma$ of order $n$, where elements are included in the generating set independently with probability $\frac{1}{2}$. We prove that the achromatic and pseudochromatic number of such a graph are both at most $\frac{(\sqrt{3}+o(1))n}{\sqrt{\log_2 n}}$ with high probability.
item.dc:creator: Craig Timmons

item.title: Frozen colorings and recolorability of blowups
item.description: arXiv:2610.27527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The $k$-reconfiguration graph $R_k(G)$ of the proper $k$-colorings of a graph $G$ is the graph whose vertices are the $k$-colorings of $G$, with an edge between two colorings if they differ on exactly one vertex. A graph $G$ is recolorable if $R_k(G)$ is connected for all $k \ge \chi(G) + 1$. In this paper, we study recolorability under blowups through frozen colorings, here blowup means replacing vertices with non-empty cliques. We characterize frozen colorings of a blowup of $G$ in terms of maximal independent sets of the base graph, and develop a lifting principle that transfers suitable frozen obstructions from an induced subgraph to a blowup of the ambient graph. This framework yields several consequences. In particular, we answer negatively a question of Belavadi, Cameron and Sintiari on recoloring via modular decomposition, and disprove their conjecture on blowups of prime graphs. We further determine exactly which cycles have all blowups recolorable: this holds for $C_n$ if and only if $n\in\{3,4,5,7\}$. The frozen obstructions arising from the negative cases, together with the lifting principle, imply that if every blowup of a graph $G$ is recolorable, then every induced hole of $G$ has length $4$, $5$, or $7$. Finally, using linear programming duality, we show that every such graph $G$ is fractionally co-strongly perfect.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Huang, Yulai Ma, Jiaqi Zhang

item.title: A proof of Vince's conjecture on the average order of connected induced subgraphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the average order of connected induced subgraphs of a connected simple graph of order $n$ and minimum degree at least $3$ is strictly greater than $n/2$, which settles a conjecture of Vince~[\emph{J. Graph Theory} 97 (2021), 82--103]. We go further and show that, for connected simple graphs of order $n$ and minimum degree exactly $k\ge3$, $K_k\vee(K_1\cup K_{n-k-1})$ uniquely minimizes this average under additional conditions.
item.dc:creator: Jungang Chen, Hongxia Ma

item.title: On minimum-size matroid counterexamples to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.27706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a matroid and let $\Tutte_M(x,y)$ be its Tutte polynomial. The multiplicative Merino--Welsh inequality \[ \Tutte_M(2,0)\Tutte_M(0,2)\geq \Tutte_M(1,1)^2 \] was proved to be false for matroids by Beke, Cs\'aji, Csikv\'ari, and Pituk (\emph{Adv. Math.} \textbf{446} (2024), 109674). Let $U_{n,r}$ denote the rank-$r$ uniform matroid on $n$ elements, where $0<r<n$, and let $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ denote the matroid obtained by replacing each element of $U_{n,r}$ with $q$ parallel copies. They constructed an infinite family of counterexamples of the form $U_{n,r}^{(2)}$, including $U_{33,22}^{(2)}$. In this paper, we prove that every $U_{n,r}^{(q)}$ with $q\geq3$ satisfies the inequality. For $q=2$, we prove that the minimum number of elements in such a counterexample is $62$, attained by $U_{31,21}^{(2)}$. For loopless and bridgeless graphs, Noble and Royle (\emph{Eur. J. Comb.} \textbf{38} (2014), 24--35) showed that every edge of a minimum-size counterexample to the multiplicative Merino--Welsh conjecture lies in a series or parallel class of size two or three. For matroids, we further prove that every element of a minimum-size loopless and coloopless counterexample lies in exactly one series or parallel class of size two.
item.dc:creator: Jungang Chen, Xian'an Jin, Tianlong Ma

item.title: Size and spectral radius conditions for the existence of $k$-factor in graphs with given minimum degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.27783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, characterizing the conditions for the existence of an $[a,b]$-factor in graphs has received significant academic attention. For integers $b\ge a\ge 1$, an $[a, b]$-factor of a graph $G$ is defined as a spanning subgraph $H$ such that $a\le d_{H}(v)\le b$ for every $v\in V(G)$. If $a=b=k$, a $[k, k]$-factor is called a $k$-factor of $G$. Let $\delta(G)$ denote the minimum degree of a graph $G$. Hao and Li [Electron. J. Combin. (2024)] posed the problem of characterizing the size or spectral radius conditions for a graph to contain an $[a,b]$-factor with $\delta(G)\ge a$. Fan, Lin and Zhu [Discrete Math. (2026)] solved the size version of this problem for the case $a < b.$ In this paper, for $a=b=k$, we characterize the size condition for a graph to have a $k$-factor with $\delta(G)\ge k$. Using this result, we also characterize the spectral radius and distance spectral radius conditions for a graph to have a $k$-factor, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Zengzhao Xu, Bo Deng, Ligong Wang

item.title: Ehrhart positivity of smooth polytopes with few facets
item.description: arXiv:2610.27819v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each dimension $d$, we determine the minimum number of facets of a smooth $d$-dimensional lattice polytope whose Ehrhart polynomial has at least one negative coefficient. This minimum is six in dimension $d=3$, seven in dimension $d=4$, and $d+2$ in every dimension $d\ge 5$. The lower bounds follow from the classification of smooth lattice polytopes with at most $d+2$ facets, together with explicit formulas for Ehrhart polynomials in dimensions at most $4$. We also prove that a lattice polytope of dimension at least $3$ with a smooth vertex cannot be $2$-integral with respect to any ordered lattice basis.
item.dc:creator: Feihu Liu, Jinlong Tang, Sihao Tao, Zihao Zhang

item.title: Almost entropic matroids and $(k,L)$-systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.27892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For an integer $k$ and a set of integers $L$, a $(k,L)$-system is a family of $k$-element sets such that the size of the intersection of any two distinct members belongs to $L$. Let $m(n,k,L)$ denote the maximum size of a $(k,L)$-system on a ground set of $n$ elements. In this work, we establish a close connection between the asymptotic growth of $m(n,k,L)$ and almost entropic matroids. As a consequence, we obtain a general computable upper bound on the asymptotics of $m(n,k,L)$ that unifies and strengthens all previously known upper bounds.
item.dc:creator: Andrey Kupavskii, Nikolai Terekhov

item.title: Functions determining few direction: the final missing case
item.description: arXiv:2610.28002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By results of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme and Sz\H{o}nyi, and of Ball, if a function $f: {\mathbb F}_q\to{\mathbb F}_q$ determines fewer than $(q+3)/2$ directions, then $f-f(0)$ is linear over a subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$, except possibly when $q$ is even and $f$ determines exactly $q/2+1$ directions. We settle this case: $f-f(0)$ is then additive. Hence every small minimal blocking set of R\'edei type in PG(2,$q$) is linear.
item.dc:creator: Peter Sziklai

item.title: Intersecting families with large covering number - On a conjecture of Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige
item.description: arXiv:2610.28029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stability theorems on intersecting families are often formulated via the covering number of set families. Let $M(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F\subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ with covering number $t$. It is known that for any fixed $t$ and fixed $k$ sufficiently large relative to $t$, one has $M(n,k,t)=(p_{t-1}(k)+o(1))(k)\binom{n}{k}$ as $n$ tends to infinity, where $p_{t-1}(k)$ is the maximum number of covers of size $t-1$ that a $k$-uniform intersecting family can have provided its covering number is $t-1$. Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured that $p_t(k)=k^t-\binom{t}{2}k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$ for fixed $t$ as $k$ tends to infinity and they also showed that $p_t(k)=k^t-b(t)k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$, where $b(t)$ is defined as the extremum of the following minimization problem. Suppose a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F$ of covering number $t$ can be partitioned into $\mathcal F_1,\dots,\mathcal F_t$ such that for every $i$ there exists a set $X_i$ with $X_i \subseteq F_i$ for all $F_i\in\mathcal F_i$ and the $X_i$'s are pairwise disjoint and non-empty. Then $b(t)$ is the minimum of $\sum_{i=1}^t(k-|X_i|)$ over all such families, partitions and $X_i$'s. In accordance with the conjecture on $p_t(k)$, Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured $b(t)=\binom{t}{2}$ for all $t\ge 2$ and proved $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\lfloor \frac{t-1}{2}\rfloor^{3/2}\le b(t)\le \binom{t}{2}$. In this note, we present a counterexample to the conjecture showing $b(t)\le 2\sqrt2\,t^{3/2}\sqrt{\log t}$ $+O(t^{3/2})$ and improve the lower bound to $\frac{2}{3^{3/4}}t^{3/2}-O(t)\le b(t)$. The counterexample was found by ChatGPT 6.1Sol, the lower bound proof is due to the human author.
item.dc:creator: Bal\'azs Patk\'os

item.title: Logarithmic edge-length ratios for planar drawings of 2-trees
item.description: arXiv:2610.28030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a planar graph $G$ with at least one edge, let $\rho(G)$ be the infimum of the ratio of the longest to the shortest edge length over all planar straight-line drawings of $G$. We prove that every $n$-vertex $2$-tree $G$ satisfies $\rho(G)\le4+5\lfloor\log_2(2n-3)\rfloor$. This improves the known $O(\sqrt n)$ upper bound and, together with the lower bound of Bla\v{z}ej, Fiala and Liotta, shows that the maximum of $\rho(G)$ over $n$-vertex $2$-trees is $\Theta(\log n)$. The proof adapts Biedl's recursive bar construction using nonintegral heights and applies a height-preserving straightening theorem.
item.dc:creator: Zahra Sabaei, Yasmin Tousinejad, Fatemeh Emami

item.title: Balanced subgraph counts and quasirandomness: a proof of the Janson--S\'os conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.28124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $0<p\leq1$, a graph sequence is $p$-quasirandom if every fixed finite simple graph $H$ has limiting labelled subgraph density $p^{|E(H)|}$. Janson and S\'os [\emph{European J. Combin.} (2015)] conjectured that, for every finite simple graph $F$ with at least two edges, $p$-quasirandomness is characterized by the random-graph asymptotics of the symmetrized counts of copies of $F$ across every balanced partition into $|V(F)|$ classes. In this paper, we prove this conjecture for all such $F$, including those with isolated vertices.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Linlin Wang, Jun Yue

item.title: Fourier Decomposition and E-Eigenvalues of Hypergraph Polynomials over Finite Abelian Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H=(V,E)$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph with polynomial $f_H(\bm{x})=\sum_{e\in E}\prod_{v\in e}x_v$. For a finite abelian group $G$ and a subgroup $S$ of $G$, the $k$-partite Cayley hypergraph $K$ has $k$ disjoint vertex parts, each indexed by $G$, and $\{(1,g_1),\ldots,(k,g_k)\}$ is an edge if and only if $g_1+\cdots+g_k\in S$. For $k=2$, $K$ is isomorphic to the Bi-Cayley graph associated with $G$ and $S$. For $k\ge3$, we use character theory to express $f_K$, under a complex unitary change of variables, as a sum of exactly $[G:S]$ nonzero monomials in pairwise disjoint sets of variables. This yields a direct sum decomposition whenever $S$ is a proper subgroup of $G$. When $G=\Z_2^m$, this transformation is real and orthogonal, enabling us to determine the complete sets of complex E-eigenvalues and Z-eigenvalues of the adjacency tensor of $K$.
item.dc:creator: Yan-Hong Bao, Yi-Zheng Fan, Lili Liao

item.title: Sharp Euler-factor positivity for the BG-rank-refined five-core crank
item.description: arXiv:2610.28186v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we complete the resolution of Stanton's problem OPAC--005 by proving its fixed-BG-rank assertion. We further establish a sharp nine-factor positivity theorem for the joint generating function. Let $K_{n,j}(z)$ enumerate partitions of $5n+4$ with BG-rank $j$ by the integer five-core crank prescribed in OPAC--005, and put $[5]_z=1+z+z^2+z^3+z^4$. We prove that $K_{n,j}(z)/[5]_z$ has nonnegative integer Laurent coefficients for every $n\ge0$ and $j\in \mathbb Z$. The refined equidistribution theorem of Berkovich and Garvan gives divisibility; the new assertion is coefficientwise nonnegativity. Set $\Psi(u,z,q)=\sum_{n\ge0}\sum_{j\in \mathbb Z}q^{n+1}u^jK_{n,j}(z)$ and $D(q)=\prod_{d\ge1}(1-q^{2d})$. For every nonnegative integer $M$, we show that $D(q)^M\Psi(u,z,q)/[5]_z$ has nonnegative coefficients if and only if $M\le9$. Thus positivity survives after removing nine of the ten partition factors supplied by the core--quotient decomposition. A coefficient equal to $-4$ at $M=10$ proves sharpness. The key step is a compensation between lattice terms of different core sizes that preserves both the BG-rank and the full integer crank. Theta identities and three local coefficient inequalities provide the required nonnegative contributions, and an explicit allocation ensures that none is used twice. The resulting factorization also yields a nine-color convolution and coefficientwise finite-difference inequalities through order nine.
item.dc:creator: Huan Xiong

item.title: On the MDS conjecture in even characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.28208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every nontrivial linear $[n,k]$ maximum distance separable (MDS) code over a finite field $\F_q$ of characteristic two satisfies $n\le q+1$, except in dimensions $k=3$ and $k=q-1$, where $n\le q+2$. This resolves the linear MDS conjecture in even characteristic.
item.dc:creator: Bocong Chen, Jing Huang

item.title: Secure Domination in Odd-order Sierpinski Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.28222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A nonempty vertex set D of a graph is secure if and only if, for every nonempty subset X of D, the closed neighborhood of X contains at least as many vertices of D as vertices outside D. A secure dominating set is a set that is both secure and dominating, and the secure domination number is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Previous work determined the secure domination number of Sierpinski graphs S_n k for even k and for odd k when n = 2. The exact values for odd k and n\geq3 remained open. In this paper, we determine these remaining values.
item.dc:creator: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng, Dehui Wang

item.title: Extremal graphs without cycles of length 0 modulo 4
item.description: arXiv:2610.28225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a remarkable recent result, Gy\H{o}ri, Li, Salia, Tompkins, Varga and Zhu determined the maximum size in a graph of given order and containing no cycle of length divisible by 4. In this paper, we give a complete characterization of all graphs attaining this maximum. This answers a question posed by Li, Pan and Shi. Very recently, Chu, Park and Ryu established a sharp upper bound on the number of edges in a 2-connected graph containing no cycle of length divisible by 4. We also give a complete characterization of all such graphs attaining this bound.
item.dc:creator: Yanan Hu, Leilei Zhang

item.title: A Complete Dichotomy for $L_\infty$ Permutation Removal
item.description: arXiv:2610.28271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the removal problem for permutation patterns under the normalized $L_\infty$ earth mover's distance. We prove a complete dichotomy. Let \[ \mathcal E =\{(12),(21),(132),(213),(231),(312)\}. \] If $\sigma\in\mathcal E$, then every permutation of length $n$ that is $\varepsilon$-far from being $\sigma$-free contains at least $\varepsilon(n-1)$ copies of $\sigma$; for $0<\varepsilon\le 1/16$, this is sharp up to a constant factor for all sufficiently large $n$. If $\sigma\in S_k\setminus\mathcal E$, then for every sufficiently large $n$ there is a permutation of length $n$ that is $1/(8k)$-far from being $\sigma$-free and contains exactly one copy of $\sigma$. Thus the usual positive-density removal conclusion fails for every nontrivial permutation pattern, but the sparse behavior is completely characterized: the minimum number of copies is linear for exactly six patterns and is one for all others. Consequently, no canonical one-sided tester that rejects only after finding a forbidden copy can have query complexity independent of the permutation length.
item.dc:creator: Viet Hung Le, Ruilin Shi, Fan Wei

item.title: Ordered Trees with Linear Off-Diagonal Ramsey Numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.28299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize the following three classes of ordered trees: $\qquad$ (1) trees $T$ satisfying $R_<(T,K_n)=O(n)$; $\qquad$ (2) $\chi$-bounding trees; $\qquad$ (3) Ramsey-good trees. In particular, we show that the first two classes coincide. The second characterization answers a question of Axenovich, Rollin and Ueckerdt, and the third resolves a problem of Balko and Poljak. In our proof, we also introduce several novel constructions of ordered graphs with sublinear independence number, giving lower bounds on $R_<(F,K_n)$ for various ordered forests $F$.
item.dc:creator: Lior Gishboliner, Artur Kravtsov, Xiangyu Li

item.title: An Erd\H{o}s-Szekeres-Type Result on Permutation Patterns
item.description: arXiv:2610.28305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an infinite set of patterns $(p,q)$ where $p$ is an almost increasing permutation and $q$ is an almost decreasing permutation, such that the exponential growth rate of permutations avoiding $(p,q)$ is 2. This extends a classical result of Erd\H{o}s and Szekeres.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Van Nimwegen

item.title: Avoiding abelian squares with three colours in the continuous setting
item.description: arXiv:2610.28376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An $n$-colouring of the real line is a Lebesgue measurable function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to A$, where $A$ is a set of $n$ colours. An abelian square for $f$ is a finite interval $U\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ where every colour shows up in the left and in the right half of $U$ with exactly the same Lebesgue measure. It is known that every $2$-colouring contains an abelian square. On the other hand, Alon, Grytczuk, Laso{\'n}, and Micha{\l}ek (2009) proved that there exist $4$-colourings that avoid abelian squares, while the question for $3$-colourings remained open. We construct a $3$-colouring that avoids abelian squares, disproving a conjecture of Laso{\'n} (2015). However, in contrast to the case of 4-colourings, the set of 3-colourings that avoid abelian squares is meagre. We show this using an argument based on the KKM lemma.
item.dc:creator: Ville Salo, Ingrid Vukusic, Charlie Wilson

item.title: On complete morphisms of Butson Hadamard matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.28394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complete morphism of Butson classes replaces each entry of a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(n,k)$ by an $m \times m$ block, uniformly, to produce a matrix in $\mathrm{BH}(mn,t)$. We show that every complete morphism is described by a pair $(U,Z)$, where $Z \in \mathrm{BH}(m,t)$ and $U$ is a unitary matrix annihilated by the $k^{\textrm{th}}$ cyclotomic polynomial. We deduce from a theorem of Lam and Leung that complete morphisms onto real Hadamard matrices exist precisely when $k$ is a power of $2$. The exponent-reducing morphisms of \"Osterg\aa rd--Paavola and \'O Cath\'ain--Swartz achieve the smallest block size the degree bound allows, and we show that there are no other complete morphisms for which $U$ is monomial. We construct new complete morphisms where $U$ is not monomial: a complete morphism $\mathrm{BH}(n,7) \rightarrow \mathrm{BH}(6n,6)$ is given, the first to eliminate a prime from the alphabet.
item.dc:creator: Ronan Egan, P\'adraig \'O Cath\'ain

item.title: Sprinkling for random regular graphs and Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.28395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the uniform random $d$-regular graph model on $n$ vertices is, in total variation distance, asymptotically close to the union of $d$ uniformly random edge-disjoint perfect matchings, provided that $n$ is even and $\omega(1) = d \leq n^{1/10}$. This confirms a conjecture by Hollom, Lichev, Mond, Portier, and Wang for this range of parameters. This result has a couple of interesting consequences. First, this shows that random $d$-regular graphs on $n$ vertices exhibit sprinkling properties for some range of parameters, thereby confirming a conjecture by Isaev, McKay, Southwell and Zhukovskii in that range. Second, we give a short alternative proof of the upper side of Kim-Vu's sandwich conjecture in the sparse regime.
item.dc:creator: Julien Portier

item.title: Forbidden graded posets in middle levels: supersaturation, enumeration and randomness
item.description: arXiv:2610.28413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P$ be a fixed finite poset whose maximal chains all have $h$ elements, and let $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ be the union of $h$ consecutive middle levels of $2^{[n]}$. We prove that the maximum size of a $P$-free subfamily of $\mathcal W_{n,h}$ is $(\pi(P)+o(1))M_n$ for a constant $\pi(P)$, where $M_n=\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, and that the number of $P$-free subfamilies is $2^{(\pi(P)+o(1))M_n}$. For connected $P$ we prove supersaturation above $(\pi(P)+\epsilon)M_n$ and determine, in terms of the coordinate patterns of the copies of $P$ in the window, a range of $p$ in which the largest $P$-free subfamily of the random family $\mathcal W_{n,h}(p)$ has size $(\pi(P)+o(1))pM_n$ and a range in which it has size $(h+o(1))pM_n$; the two ranges meet whenever all copies have the same pattern. For the Boolean poset $Q_d$, which has height $d+1$, the threshold order in the corresponding window $\mathcal W_{n,d+1}$ is $n^{-d/(2^d-1)}$, and $\pi_d=\pi(Q_d)$ satisfies $(d+1)\lambda_d\le\pi_d\le d+1-\binom d{\lfloor d/2\rfloor}^{-1}$, where $\lambda_d$ is the vertex Tur\'an density of $d$-dimensional subcubes in the hypercube. Together with a construction of Ellis, Ivan and Leader this gives $d+1-\pi_d=\exp(-\Theta(d))$. For the diamond, known bounds give $2.1479\le\pi_2\le2.15121$.
item.dc:creator: Jiangdong Ai, Mingyu Liu, Zhiyu Song

item.title: Independent transversals in hypergraphs with low codegrees
item.description: arXiv:2610.28468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every fixed $r\geq3$, $k>0$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there is $\gamma>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $b$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ whose vertex set is partitioned into parts of size at least $b$ contains at least $\lceil(1-\varepsilon)b\rceil$ pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals, provided that the average degree in each part is at most $kb^{r-1}$ and maximum $j$-codegree $\Delta_j(\mathcal H)\leq\gamma b^{r-j}$ for $2\leq j<r$. Under the same average degree, if $q$ is the minimum part size and $\Delta_j(\mathcal H)=o(q^{r-j})$ for $2\leq j<r$, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint independent transversals is $(1-o(1))q$ as $q\to\infty$. We develop an iterative halving reduction for partitioned hypergraphs to apply the theorem of Delcourt and Postle on matchings avoiding forbidden submatchings.
item.dc:creator: Hanle Dai, Luyining Gan

item.title: A sharp bound on the binding number of $K_k$-free graphs and the Brandt conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.28536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The binding number of a graph is the smallest ratio $|N(S)|/|S|$ among all nonempty vertex sets $S$ whose neighborhood $N(S)$ is not the whole vertex set. We prove that every finite nonempty $K_k$-free graph has binding number at most $k-2$ for every $k\ge6$, confirming Brandt's conjecture; the bound is sharp for complete $(k-1)$-partite graphs with equal nonempty parts. We first prove the case $k=6$ and then extend it to all $k\ge6$ by induction.
item.dc:creator: Jifu Lin, Heng Yang

item.title: Extremal secant size distributions in projective planes
item.description: arXiv:2610.28541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a point set $S$ in a projective plane of order $q$, each line $\ell$ determines a secant of size $|S\cap \ell|$. We study how concentrated this secant-size distribution can be. We develop a general framework for estimating and, in several cases, determining the extremal number. We point out how the extremal constructions vary depending on the remainder of the size of the set modulo $q$, and classify several extremal families of point sets, building from concurrent lines, Baer {subplanes} and lines in general position. On the lower bound side, we rely on stability results in the Desarguesian case and applications of the standard equalities in general. Finally, we connect the problem to a novel concept, called general position on level 2 for point and line sets, which then leads to a Sidon-type problem over finite fields called projective Sidon sets, providing an additional arithmetic model for highly concentrated secant-size distributions.
item.dc:creator: Zolt\'an L\'or\'ant Nagy, Zsuzsa Weiner

item.title: Vanishing Uniform Tur\'an Densities: Characterization and Jumps
item.description: arXiv:2610.28574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uniform Tur\'an density problems ask for the minimum density threshold that guarantees a copy of a fixed 3-uniform hypergraph $F$ in every sufficiently large 3-uniform hypergraph whose edges are uniformly distributed. This line of research was initiated by Erd\H{o}s and S\'os in the 1980s, who introduced the notion of \emph{vertex-set Tur\'an density} $\pi_{vvv}(F)$. Reiher, R\"odl and Schacht later defined two related concepts, namely, the \emph{vertex-pair Tur\'an density} $\pi_{ve}(F)$ and the \emph{cherry Tur\'an density} $\pi_{ee}(F)$, which satisfy the chain of inequalities $\pi_{vvv}(F)\ge\pi_{ve}(F)\ge\pi_{ee}(F)$. In this paper, we investigate the problem for their vanishing densities. First, we characterize the 3-uniform hypergraphs $F$ for which $\pi_{ee}(F)=0$, thereby answering a question posed by Schacht. We show that these are precisely the so-called \emph{max-layered} 3-uniform hypergraphs recently introduced by Lamaison. Furthermore, we answer an analogous question of Lamaison for the \emph{minimum-codegree palette density} $\pi_{ee}^{\rm pal}$. Together, these results imply that the following are equivalent: $\pi_{ee}(F)=0$, $\pi_{ee}^{\rm pal}(F)=0$, and $F$ is a max-layered 3-uniform hypergraph. Let $\star \in \{vvv, ve, ee \}$. We say that zero is a \emph{jump} for $\pi_{\star}$ if there exists $c>0$ such that no $3$-uniform hypergraph $F$ satisfies $\pi_{\star}(F)\in(0,c)$. A famous result of Reiher, R\"odl and Schacht asserts that zero is a jump for $\pi_{vvv}$. In contrast, we prove that zero is not a jump for either $\pi_{ve}$ or $\pi_{ee}$. This also yields a negative answer to Schacht's well-ordering question for $\pi_{ve}$. Together with existing results, these findings complete the picture for all three notions of uniform Tur\'an density at zero.
item.dc:creator: Hao Lin, Jie Ma, Wenling Zhou

item.title: Inscribed 4-polytopes of maximal volume with seven and eight vertices
item.description: arXiv:2610.26886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove, with sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, that every cyclic $4$-polytope with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $2/5$. Hence no $4$-polytope of maximal volume with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ is cyclic, answering a question of Horv\'ath and L\'angi for $d = 4$, and with their theorem the maximal volume is $\sqrt{3}/4$. With eight vertices, the same method bounds the volume of every simplicial type other than the cross-polytope by $13/20$, so the regular cross-polytope, of volume $2/3$, is up to orthogonal transformations the unique maximiser.
item.dc:creator: Csaba Medgyes

item.title: Littlewood's mutually touching cylinders: the maximum is seven
item.description: arXiv:2610.26940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that eight congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ cannot touch pairwise. Since seven such cylinders exist, the maximum number of congruent mutually touching infinite cylinders is seven. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mati\'c, Rado\v{s} Radoi\v{c}i\'c, Andreas Spomer

item.title: A Geometric Principle for Path Selection in Directed Acyclic Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There are many types of path between nodes of a Directed acyclic graph (DAG), including the shortest and longest paths. Here, we ask whether the choice of path used in any analysis reflects the geometry of the latent space in which the DAG is embedded. To do this we define L_p-cube spacetimes, a family of continuous ordered spaces in which a single parameter p determines whether the ordered distance satisfies the ordered triangle identity when p>1, or the reverse ordered triangle identity when 0<p<1 or p<0, both of which are rarely studied. The forward connection kernel in the p<0 case has infinite hyper-volume, yet it is a well defined model. We then construct random geometric DAGs embedded in our L_p-cube spacetime and study their geometry. For p>1, where the ordered triangle identity holds, the shortest paths provide the closest approximation to the continuum ordered geodesic while for 0<p<1 and p<0, where the reverse ordered triangle identity holds, this role is instead taken by the longest weighted path. We also test the robustness of this relationship in a geometric citation model in which the random geometric DAG is supplemented by a preferential-attachment-type mechanism allowing connections beyond the strict geometric cut-off. The same broad correspondence between latent geometry and ordered geodesic path type is recovered. Our results show that the preference for shortest or longest paths in a DAG is closely connected to the geometry assumed for its latent space, and suggest that path structure can provide information about latent geometry, even when that geometry is not directly observed.
item.dc:creator: Haya AlMuhanna, Tim S. Evans

item.title: Short Point Lists for CNFs and Stronger Constant-Depth Circuit Hardness
item.description: arXiv:2610.27127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a short-description decomposition of bounded-width CNFs. For every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, every width-$b$ CNF on $m$ variables is an exact disjoint union of at most $2^{\varepsilon m}$ width-$b$ CNFs, each determined by $2^{O_\varepsilon(b)}\log(m+1)$ satisfying assignments. For every fixed $d\ge3$, we prove a worst-case size lower bound of $2^{\Omega_d((n\log n)^{1/(d-1)})}$ against depth-at-most-$d$ unbounded-fan-in AND/OR circuits with input negations for three polynomial-time Boolean families: inverse trace over binary fields, the Goldreich--Tal trilinear function, and OpenAI's polynomial evaluator with its original parameters. All parameter bits count as inputs. For inverse trace, every such circuit of size at most $S$, where $n\le S\le2^{c_dn^{1/(d-1)}}$, has uniform sign correlation at most $2^{-\eta_dn\log\log S/(\log S)^{d-1}}$. Here $c_d,\eta_d>0$ depend only on $d$. This improves on the classical parity correlation bound. The lower bounds combine the decomposition with restriction arguments; the correlation bound additionally uses common partial decision trees. We also construct exact nonuniform AND/OR circuits for inverse trace of size $2^{O(n^{2/3})}$ at depth eight and $2^{O(\sqrt n\log n)}$ at depth nine. For every fixed integer $h\ge2$, the construction gives depth-$(4h+1)$ circuits of size $2^{O_h(n^{1/h}\log n)}$. The upper bounds implement finite-field evaluation and interpolation using circuits that enumerate intermediate states.
item.dc:creator: Xin Li, Yan Zhong

item.title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
item.description: arXiv:2610.27166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $\theta=\beta/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $N\theta\to\gamma>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/\theta$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $\gamma$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $\beta$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $\gamma\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Jiaming Xu

item.title: A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.27457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the graphon variational problem that governs lower tail large deviations of the number of copies of a fixed nonbipartite graph $H$ in a sparse Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graph. Our main new insight is that any non-constant minimizer of the variational problem exhibits a discontinuous jump away from the constant graphon. We deduce that the replica-symmetric and symmetry-breaking regimes are separated by a single critical parameter and that the phase transition is first order. In the supercritical regime $p \gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, we transfer these results to the conditioned random graph, showing that the edge density is a discontinuous order parameter and that the conditioned graph concentrates in cut distance near the full minimizer set.
item.dc:creator: Byron Chin

item.title: Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.27481v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: $\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.
item.dc:creator: Takuya Murakami

item.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.
item.dc:creator: Rusiru Gambheera

item.title: On Hankel Determinantal Matroids
item.description: arXiv:2610.27554v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We initiate a study of the algebraic matroid associated to the ideal generated by the $(r+1)$-minors of a Hankel matrix of variables. We prove that this matroid is uniform, that is, a coordinate projection from the corresponding Hankel determinantal variety is generically finite if and only if it preserves at least $2r$ anti-diagonals. For such projections, we establish bounds on the degree. These results are of significance to the problem of Hankel low-rank matrix completion.
item.dc:creator: Ethan Reed, Manolis C. Tsakiris

item.title: Almgren minimality of products of simplex-skeleton cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.27845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we prove that for every $m,n\geq 2$, the orthogonal product $S_m\times S_n\subset\R^m\times\R^n$ is an Almgren minimal cone of dimension $m+n-2$, where $S_k\subset\R^k$ is the cone over the $(k-2)$-skeleton of a regular $k$-simplex. Lawlor and Morgan \cite{LM94} proved the minimality of each $S_k$ by paired calibrations, while Guy David \cite{DJT, GD13} later raised the general question whether products of Almgren minimal sets remain minimal. Our theorem gives a affirmative answer to this product question within the entire Lawlor-Morgan regular-simplex family. It extends the isolated example \(\Y\times \Y\), the product of two 1-dimensional $\Y$ sets, proved in 2014 by the second author, simultaneously to all pairwise products \(S_m\times S_n\), and therefore produces a large new family of possible codimension-two singularities for Plateau's problem. The key idea of the proof is to find a new way to combine homology with paired calibrations in higher codimension. Instead of using only the currents associated with the facets, we consider all their nonzero $\FF$ combinations. The resulting complete family has enough algebraic symmetry to control uniformly the overlaps created by noninjective deformations.
item.dc:creator: Songsong Huang, Xiangyu Liang, Zaoyi Zhang

item.title: Solid-angle formulas for simplicial cones and random shifted sections of polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.28084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider simplicial cones $C = \operatorname{pos}(v_1, \ldots, v_n) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose generators have a Gram matrix of the form $(\langle v_i, v_j \rangle)_{i,j=1}^n = \operatorname{Id}_n+\sum_{j=1}^p \lambda_j u_j u_j^T$, where $p\in \{0,\ldots, n\}$, $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p > -1$ and $u_1,\ldots, u_p \in \mathbb{R}^n$ are orthogonal unit vectors. We derive an explicit $p$-dimensional integral formula for the solid angle of $C$ involving the analytic continuation of the standard normal distribution function. As an application, explicit formulas are obtained for the expected face numbers of sections of acute orthocentric simplices and crosspolytopes with uniformly distributed linear subspaces translated by a fixed vector. The translation vector is assumed to lie outside the affine hulls of all proper faces of the polytope. All solid angles entering these formulas are expressed as integrals of dimension at most two. This application includes regular simplices and regular crosspolytopes as special cases.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Schange

item.title: Berry--Esseen Bounds for Faces in Unimodular Triangulations of Random Polytopes
item.description: arXiv:2610.28088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Consider the number of faces arising from unimodular triangulations of random polytopes associated with Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi graphs. Focusing on two-dimensional faces of regular unimodular triangulations of random symmetric edge polytopes, we derive precise asymptotic expansions for the expectation and variance and then establish a quantitative central limit theorem with an explicit Berry--Esseen bound. The proof combines an algebraically derived characterization of faces in terms of local graph configurations with a detailed combinatorial--geometric study of the relevant configurations. The normal approximation is established using the discrete Malliavin--Stein method. We also determine the asymptotic orders of the expectation and variance and establish a quantitative central limit theorem for the number of faces in each fixed higher dimension. These results identify a common local mechanism underlying the fluctuations of face numbers and extend the distributional theory of random symmetric edge polytopes [Donzelmann et al., arXiv:2603.10650] beyond edge statistics.
item.dc:creator: Zhonggen Su, Huilian Zheng

item.title: Simultaneous popular differences for polynomial and linear progressions in finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.28226v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study simultaneous popular differences for polynomial progressions and linear progressions over finite fields $\mathbb F_p$. For certain families of polynomial progressions of algebraic complexity $1$, such as $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^3, x+2y^3)$, we prove the existence of $y \neq 0$ which is popular simultaneously for both progressions. This extends previous results by Conlon, Dong and Hong who considered complexity $0$ progressions. On the other hand, we construct counterexamples showing that simultaneous popular differences are not guaranteed to exist for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^2, x+2y^2)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y, x+3y)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x,x+y,x+2y,x+3y)$, answering questions posed by Conlon, Dong and Hong.
item.dc:creator: Xuancheng Shao, Weiwen Zhang

item.title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.28504v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Badger

item.title: New Newton-type inequality and a unified perspective on Maclaurin's inequality via the inclusion relations of cones
item.description: arXiv:2610.28544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The classical Newton-Maclaurin's inequalities for the elementary symmetric means are well known. In this paper, we derive a new class of Newton-type inequalities and generalize Maclaurin's inequality by connecting the elementary symmetric functions with their counterparts. Our idea is mainly motivated by the inclusion relations of G$\mathring{\text{a}}$rding's cones and $k$-convex cones.
item.dc:creator: Ning Cao, Xuanxuan Hu, Feida Jiang

item.title: Isolation of non-triangle cycles in graphs
item.description: arXiv:2510.08361v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a set $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs, we call a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. The $\mathcal{F}$-isolation number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\iota(G, \mathcal{F})$, is the size of a smallest set $D$ of vertices of $G$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $\mathcal{F}$-graphs contained by $G$ (equivalently, $G-N[D]$ contains no $\mathcal{F}$-graph). Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the set of cycles, and let $\mathcal{C}'$ be the set of non-triangle cycles (that is, cycles of length at least $4$). Let $G$ be a connected graph having exactly $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. The first author proved that $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}) \leq n/4$ if $G$ is not a triangle. Bartolo and the authors determined a set $\mathcal{E}_4$ of nine graphs such that $\iota(G,\{C_4\}) \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not an $\mathcal{E}_4$-graph. Chen and Cui recently strengthened this result by proving that $\iota(G, \mathcal{C}') \leq n/5$ if $G$ is not an $\mathcal{E}_4$-graph. This had been proved by Zhang and Wu for the case where $G$ contains no triangle. Various authors proved that $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}) \leq (m+1)/5$ if $G$ is not a triangle. We prove that $\iota(G,\mathcal{C}') \leq (m+1)/6$ if $G$ is not a $4$-cycle. Zhang and Wu established this for the case where $G$ contains no triangle. Our result yields the inequality $\iota(G,\{C_4\}) \leq (m+1)/6$ of Wei, Zhang and Zhao. These bounds are attained by infinitely many (non-isomorphic) graphs. The proof of our inequality hinges on also determining the graphs attaining the bound.
item.dc:creator: Peter Borg, Dayle Scicluna

item.title: Integral quasi-strongly regular Cayley graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.14496v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quasi-strongly regular graphs form a significant generalization of strongly regular graphs. We study the eigenvalues of a family of such graphs, $\Gamma_H(G)$, constructed from a finite group $G$ and a subgroup $H$. Our main results include a sufficient condition for $\Gamma_H(G)$ to be integral and an explicit computation of its entire spectrum when $H$ is normal, revealing that the spectrum in this case depends only on $|G|$ and the index $[G:H]$.
item.dc:creator: Sauvik Poddar, Sucharita Biswas, Angsuman Das

item.title: Efficient total facial coloring of combinatorial maps
item.description: arXiv:2601.12514v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $1<k\in\mathbb{Z}$. A total coloring of a connected simple regular graph $G$ via color set $]k]_0=\{0,1,\ldots, k\}$ is efficient if each color yields an efficient dominating set, where efficient domination applies to each color class in $V(G)$. An efficient total coloring of $G$ via $[k]_0$ extends to an efficient total facial coloring $c$ of a map $M(G)$ of $G$ if it assigns a vertex-and-edge $k$-color set to the boundary cycle of each face, with the consequently missing color assigned to the face itself, so that the two adjacent faces along each edge are assigned different colors. Focus is set upon planar and toroidal maps. Modifications of $c$ are also treated by removing a perfect dominating set or a 1-factor from $G$.
item.dc:creator: Italo J. Dejter

item.title: The distinguishing number of complete bipartite and crown graphs
item.description: arXiv:2601.15913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The distinguishing number of a permutation group $G\leqslant\Sym(\Omega)$ is the minimum number of colours needed to colour $\Omega$ in such a way that the only colour preserving element of $G$ is the identity. The distinguishing number of a graph is the distinguishing number of its automorphism group (as a permutation group on vertices). We determine the distinguishing number of the complete bipartite graphs $K_{n,n}$ and the crown graphs $K_{n,n}-nK_2$, as well as the distinguishing number of some `large' subgroups of their automorphism groups, that is, the subgroups that are vertex- and edge-transitive and such that the induced action on each bipart is $\Alt(n)$ or $\Sym(n)$. We show that, if $G$ is a `large' group of automorphisms of $K_{n,n}$, then $n-1\leqslant D(G) \leqslant n+1$. Similarly, if $G$ is a `large' group of automorphisms of a crown graph, then $\lceil \sqrt{n-1}\rceil \leqslant D(G)\leqslant \lfloor \sqrt{n}\rfloor+1$. \smallskip \textit{Keywords:} complete bipartite graph; crown graph; distinguishing number; symmetric group; alternating group
item.dc:creator: Lei Chen, Alice Devillers, Luke Morgan, Friedrich Rober

item.title: The exact Erd\H{o}s-Ko-Rado Theorem for 3-wise $t$-intersecting uniform families
item.description: arXiv:2603.07991v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: One of the central problems in extremal set theory is the determination of the maximum size of an $r$-wise $t$-intersecting $k$-graph on $n$ vertices. For $r=2$ after decades of effort, a complete solution was given by the Complete Intersection Theorem (\cite{AK0}). However the case $r\geq 3$ remains wide open. The $t$-star consisting of all $k$-sets containing a fixed $t$-set provides a lower bound. For $r=3$ and $k\geq t+2\geq44$, we determine the exact threshold for which it is optimal for $n>k$. The condition is essentially $n\geq \sqrt{t}k$. For $k\geq t+2\geq47$ and $n\geq\frac{\sqrt{4t+9}-1}{2}k$, we also establish the corresponding Hilton-Milner-type stability result.
item.dc:creator: Peter Frankl, Jian Wang

item.title: Enumeration and Monotonicity of Linear Codes with Prescribed Hull Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2605.29204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The hull of a linear code is the intersection of the code with its dual and depends on the choice of inner product. We study how the numbers of linear codes with prescribed Euclidean, Hermitian, and symplectic hull dimensions vary with the hull dimension. Building on closed enumeration formulae, we derive exact ratio decompositions for the Hermitian and symplectic cases, determine the parameter ranges in which monotonicity holds, and identify the exceptional families. We also compare the three inner products and complement the theoretical analysis with computational classification results for quaternary codes.
item.dc:creator: Stefka Bouyuklieva, Iliya Bouyukliev, Keita Ishizuka, Ferruh \"Ozbudak

item.title: Counting connected multitype graphs with prescribed edge counts
item.description: arXiv:2606.17912v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the exponential asymptotics of the number of connected labelled graphs with finitely many vertex types, prescribed numbers of vertices of each type, and prescribed edge counts between each pair of types. Under an irreducibility and strict surplus condition, we express the count for linear surplus of edges as the unrestricted count multiplied by an explicit exponential connectivity factor, up to a multiplicative error \(\exp\{o(n)\}\). The factor is characterized by a finite-dimensional nonlinear system whose solution exists and is unique. We use a probabilistic method, exploiting large-deviation principles and asymptotic estimates for connectedness probabilities to relate the counting problem to the emergence of giant components in suitably tuned supercritical random graphs. For connected bipartite graphs, we determine the exponential rate throughout the regime of positive linear excess and fixed positive limiting proportions of the two vertex classes. In the parameter ranges where the existing upper and lower bounds apply, this identifies the exponential rate left undetermined by those estimates.
item.dc:creator: Luisa Andreis, Mario Veshaj

item.title: A Littlewood-Richardson Rule for Forest Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2606.23876v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The forest polynomials $\mathfrak{P}_a$ of Nadeau-Tewari form a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$ whose role for the cohomology of the quasisymmetric flag variety parallels that of Schubert polynomials for the classical flag variety. Nonnegativity of the structure constants $\beta_{a,b}^c$ in $\mathfrak{P}_a \mathfrak{P}_b = \sum_c \beta_{a,b}^c \mathfrak{P}_c$ is known, but no Littlewood-Richardson-style enumerative rule has been available. We give such a rule: $\beta_{a,b}^c$ counts pairs of forest RC graphs of forest-codes $a$ and $b$ whose lift product lands on a forest RC graph of forest-code and weight both equal to $c$. The same rule descends to the cup product on $H^\bullet(\mathrm{QFl}_n)$. The proof introduces a squash product $\boxtimes$ on RC graphs, which on full Grassmannian RC graphs of a fixed height recovers the plactic monoid, a multiplactic algebra $\mathcal{M}_n$ that models Schubert polynomial multiplication, and a lift product $*$ on RC graphs whose quasi-crystal structure, in the framework of Cain-Guilherme-Malheiro, transports the Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence through the computation. The row-decomposition machinery on RC graphs that underlies these constructions is developed in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Matthew J. Samuel

item.title: Skeleton Chordalities
item.description: arXiv:2607.21166v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study new higher-dimensional analogs of graph chordality and review the existing ones. Our main results for simplicial complexes are: (1) $\Delta$ skeleton-E-chordal $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta^\vee$ vertex-decomposable $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$ skeleton-clique-chordal. Moreover, for subflag complexes, $\Delta$ skeleton-E-chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ $\Delta^\vee$ vertex-decomposable. (For $d=1$ this boils down to ``$G$ chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ $G^\vee$ vertex-decomposable'', a result closely related to Fr\"oberg's theorem.) (2) For subflag complexes, $\Delta$ is skeleton-E-chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ it splits as $\Delta = \Delta_1 \cup \Delta_2$, with each $\Delta_i$ a skeleton-E-chordal induced subcomplex of $\Delta$, and with $\Delta_1 \cap \Delta_2$ a complex whose $1$-skeleton is a clique. (This generalizes ``$G$ chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ $G$ splits as a union of chordal graphs that intersect in a common clique''). (3) $\Delta$ skeleton-E-chordal $\Longleftrightarrow$ every nonempty induced subcomplex of $\Delta$ has a skeleton-E-simplicial vertex. (Generalizes ``$G$ chordal $\Leftrightarrow$ every nonempty induced subgraph has a simplicial vertex''.) (4) $\Delta$ underclosed $\Rightarrow$ $\Delta$ skeleton-weakly-chordal and weakly-closed. (Generalizes ``$G$ interval $\Rightarrow$ $G$ chordal and co-comparability''.) (5) All pure E-chordal complexes are vertex-chordal; all pure mid-chordal complexes are weakly-vertex-chordal; all pure very-weakly-chordal complexes are weakly-ridge-chordal. (This expands Bigdeli, Yazdan-Pour and Zaare-Nahandi's work on ridge-chordality.)
item.dc:creator: Bruno Benedetti, Marta Pavelka

item.title: Peeling sequences: a directional method for the three-block construction
item.description: arXiv:2609.19540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A peeling sequence of a finite planar point set is an ordering of its points, such that when the points get removed in this order, each removed point is a vertex of the current convex hull of the set. Write $g(S)$ for the number of such sequences, and $g(n)$ for the minimum of $g(S)$ over $n$-point sets in general position. We present a method which can be used to prove better upper bounds on the previously analysed recursive 3-block constructions $S_n$. In fact, we prove $g(n)\leq g(S_n)=O(6.57^n)$, using directional restrictions and a weighted prefix-tree form of the Kraft--McMillan inequality. From the other direction, we show that the same construction cannot attain the current best known lower bound of $c\cdot3^n$. In fact, $g(S_n)\geq 5.22^n$ when $n$ is a large enough power of $3$. Improving the general lower bound on $g(n)$ is still an open question.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel G\'abor Simon

item.title: Extremal numbers of acyclic matrices
item.description: arXiv:2609.20726v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a zero-one matrix $P$, let $\operatorname{Ex}(n,P)$ denote the maximum number of ones in an $n\times n$ zero-one matrix avoiding $P$. We prove that $$\operatorname{Ex}(n,P) \leq n^{1+O_P(1/\log\log n)}$$ for every acyclic $P$, settling the weak form of the Pach-Tardos conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Lior Gishboliner, Xiangyu Li

item.title: Exact Ehrhart Series of Birkhoff Polytopes via Constant Terms and Finite-Field Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2609.25863v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Ehrhart series of the $n$th Birkhoff polytope is $\sum_{r\geq0}H_n(r)z^r$, where $H_n(r)$ counts nonnegative integer $n\times n$ matrices whose row and column sums all equal $r$. We present an exact method for computing this series using constant terms and finite fields. A root filter expresses $H_n(r)$ as a weighted sum of the values $h_r(M)^n$, where $h_r$ is the complete homogeneous symmetric polynomial and $M$ ranges over multisets of $m$th roots of unity with $m=r+1$. Constant-term cancellation reduces the evaluation of $h_r(M)$ to a sum over repeated elements $a$ of $M$. For a particular $a$ of multiplicity $\mu_a$, the computation uses a generalized Todd coefficient of degree $\mu_a-2$. Sums of $h_r(M)^n$ over selected multiplicity classes are handled using symmetric function techniques. Together with the remaining individual evaluations, this gives $O_n(m^{n-5}+m^4)$ field operations for each admissible prime and fixed $n\geq5$. An explicit bound and the Chinese remainder theorem recover the integer counts, and Ehrhart symmetry determines the full series. The same method applies to the World Cup problem, which counts the same matrices with diagonal entries required to be $0$. We prove correctness and compute complete series for both families through order $13$. The Birkhoff series for orders $10$--$13$ and the World Cup series for orders $9$--$13$ are tabulated in the appendices.
item.dc:creator: Xinru Jiang, Guoce Xin, Chen Zhang, Yueming Zhong

item.title: There is no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph
item.description: arXiv:2609.37978v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A graph is $K_3$-irregular if its vertices belong to pairwise distinct numbers of triangles. We prove that no $8$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists, settling the last unresolved case. Following the initial discovery of such graphs for regularities $r \in \{10,11,12\}$ (Stevanovi\'c et al., 2024), our previous work (Hak et al., 2025) showed that no such graphs exist for $r \le 7$, provided the first example for $r=9$, and proved that any $8$-regular candidate must have between $17$ and $22$ vertices. We exclude these possible orders for $r=8$ by combining careful analysis of triangle degrees with integer linear programming techniques. Meanwhile, a recent construction (Zhang, 2026) established that regular $K_3$-irregular graphs do exist for all $r \ge 9$. Together with our results, this establishes that an $r$-regular $K_3$-irregular graph exists if and only if $r\geq 9$.
item.dc:creator: Artem Hak, Sergiy Kozerenko, Andrii Serdiuk

item.title: Continuous Narayana Interpolations: Hankel Total Positivity and Log-Convexity Preservation
item.description: arXiv:2610.19548v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a continuous interpolation between the type $B$ and shifted type $A$ Narayana triangles. Using a direct Gegenbauer-moment proof and a continuant comparison criterion, we show that the row polynomials form a coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive sequence for every real $\theta\ge0$, and establish the same property for the moment sequences associated with all tails of the corresponding Jacobi matrix. Their $\gamma$-expansion, real-rootedness and Stieltjes moment representation are explicit, as are the exact orders of vanishing and extreme coefficients of arbitrary Hankel minors. This confirms and strengthens Rodelet--Causse--Tevlin's log-convexity conjecture for super Narayana polynomials. We further extend Wang--Yang's total positivity of the type~$A$ and $B$ Narayana triangles and strict total positivity of the associated squares to every real $\theta>-1$, using P\'olya-frequency sequences and a gamma-product moment representation. We also prove that the continuous Narayana transformations preserve strong $t$-log-convexity for every $\theta\ge0$, and that every $d$-Hoggatt transformation has the same property for integers $d\ge1$. The preservation proofs employ the Zhu--Sun criterion and a mixed-minor one-sign-change argument based on a hypergeometric hitting-probability inequality.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Zeng

item.title: Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal for excluding paths
item.description: arXiv:2610.24887v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Erd\H{o}s-Hajnal conjecture for excluding an arbitrary path. A major step in our proof is a novel Gy\'arf\'as path argument based on the ideas of bookkeeping blockades and splitting paths, which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Tung H. Nguyen

item.title: The e-positivity of $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k(e_\mu)$
item.description: arXiv:2610.26303v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the partition division operator $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k$ preserves e-positivity, resolving a conjecture of Alexandersson and Dai. For $\mu\vdash kn$ and $\nu\vdash n$, we express the coefficient of $e_\nu$ in $\mathrm{rowDiv}_k(e_\mu)$ as a normalized sum of positive rational weights over closed walks on a finite directed graph of $k$-restricted partitions. The proof combines the Pieri rule and a root of unity factorization for Macdonald polynomials. As a corollary, we recover the h-positivity of the symmetric functions $A_{n,k}$ of Amdeberhan, Shareshian, and Stanley.
item.dc:creator: Per Alexandersson, Lilan Dai

item.title: Inference of Hierarchical Core-Periphery Structure in Temporal Networks
item.description: arXiv:2506.10135v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Networks can have various types of mesoscale structures. One such structure is core--periphery structure, which consists of sets of densely-connected core nodes and sets of sparsely-connected peripheral nodes. Core nodes are connected densely to other core nodes and are potentially connected densely to peripheral nodes, which are connected sparsely to other nodes. There has been much research on core--periphery structure in time-independent networks, but few core--periphery detection methods have been developed for time-dependent (i.e., ``temporal") networks.
